# Lute

> Lute is a statically analyzable narrative language for branching games: `.lute` documents compile to a versioned JSON IR plus CEL. Write dialogue, quests, cinematic beats, and relational world state; check reachability, simulate outcomes, and compile before you ship. The current language version is **0.39.0** and the current IR version is **0.39.0**.

Lute is deliberately non-Turing: every document is a finite, terminating artifact, so the checker can prove reachability, definite-assignment, and envelope properties instead of guessing. The CLI (`lute`) is a headless checker, compiler, and preview tool; `lute context --json` emits the project-resolved authoring surface an AI or human needs to write valid Lute, and `lute check --json` gives a machine-readable diagnostic loop. Content vocabulary is the project's, not the compiler's: since language 0.9.0 the core declares vocabulary *slots* and ships zero members (since 0.37.0 the slots are `emotion`, `action`, `anchor`, `costume`, `mood`, `volume`, `musicPlayback`, `vfxType`, and the staging domains `framing`, `cameraMove`, `transition`, `cgLayout`, `sequence`, `textStyle`), so every `emotion=`/`action=`/`::music{mood}` value must be declared by the project first — an undeclared slot is the error `E-DOMAIN-UNKNOWN`. Below, each link points to a single documentation page on <https://lute-lang.vercel.app>.

## 0.33 engine integration

Execution IR 0.33 adds compiler-derived, sorted, duplicate-free
`requiredSemantics` immediately after `capabilitySnapshot`; the project index
carries the sorted union. Engines load an immutable `lute.engine.yaml` matrix
after the exact pre-1.0 major.minor IR gate, then compare each required semantic
id with `supportedIds`. `run --engine` and `play --engine` refuse unsupported
ids before playback with exit 2 and `E-ENGINE-SEMANTICS`; malformed matrices,
unsupported IR lines, and unknown ids use `E-ENGINE-MATRIX`,
`E-ENGINE-IR-VERSION`, and `E-SEMANTICS-UNKNOWN`. `check --engine` and
`check-project --engine` perform author-time checks and report
`E-CHECK-ENGINE-SEMANTICS` with source spans. The registry is normative in
the [0.33.0 proposal](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/blob/main/docs/proposals/scenario-dsl/0.33.0.md).

## Docs

- [Installation](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/installation/): Install the Lute CLI with bunx, a global bun install, or from Rust source, then verify the toolchain and move on to your first scene.
- [Try Lute (playground)](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/playground/): A fully client-side browser playground — the Lute core compiled to WebAssembly — with live diagnostics, the compiled JSON IR, and a mock-driven trace over one self-contained core-profile document.
- [Write your first scene](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/first-scene/): Build one small, real Lute scene from an empty file step by step, running the lute tool at every step to see exactly what it reports, then pin it with a test.
- [Connect scenes into a story](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/connect-scenes/): Chain scenes into a whole story you can play and test without a game engine — one made-up occasion answered by every scene, after for the order, priority for the running order, when for branching endings, and a play script for lute play.
- [Learning paths](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/learning-paths/): Role-first routes through the Lute docs — pick the reading order that matches what you are here to do, whether you write scenarios, program narrative logic, integrate an engine, author a plugin, or build AI tooling.
- [Build an investigation](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/build-an-investigation/): A first-project tutorial that builds a small whodunit in a folder of your own, file by file — project manifest, schema, facts and Datalog, three scenes with an interrogation hub, a quest, after-sequencing, check-project and its relational guard analysis, scenario reach, two trace mocks, scenario tests, and compile.
- [Is Lute right for you?](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/getting-started/when-to-use/): Honest selection guidance — the projects and teams Lute fits well today, and the ones it does not fit yet, so you can decide before you invest.
- [Cheatsheet](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/reference/cheatsheet/): One page to keep open while writing Lute 0.29.0 (with its clock, quest structure, parties, bridge answers, exclusive relations, shared spends, quest graph edges, kinds assembled with add:, kind targets, directive when=, component defaults and @@who, rule counts, engine gates, terminal states and persistent endings, finite clocks, weeks, seasons, rearm and a latching spentBy, beat templates, chapters, labels, label forms and plurals, hub return blocks, and follows= / outcome= / visibleWhen=): every construct with a minimal checked snippet (project layout, frontmatter, lines, choices, match, state, CEL, beats, clock, quests, lore, components, timelines), the CLI at a glance, the diagnostics authors hit most, and the gotchas.
- [Diagnostics reference](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/reference/diagnostics/): Every diagnostic code Lute reports: what raises it, and the spec sections behind it.
- [Reserved names](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/reference/reserved-names/): The names Lute keeps for itself, where each is refused, and what to write instead.
- [Many authors, one project](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/guides/multi-author/): How a lead and several area writers share one Lute project: ownership by directory, kinds assembled with add:, defaults, id conventions, contract beats, hand-off plays, and the merge gates that catch what collides.
- [Coming from Ink or Yarn](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/guides/coming-from-ink-yarn/): A map from Ink and Yarn Spinner to Lute: knots and nodes, diverts and jumps, choices and loops, variables, conditional text, sequences, endings, comments and tags, and what the checker says when Ink or Yarn syntax slips into a .lute file.
- [Frontmatter & profiles](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/frontmatter-and-profiles/): The YAML frontmatter block that opens every .lute document — required and optional keys, plus the profile/plugins capability selectors.
- [Content vocabulary](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/vocabulary/): The compiler declares the content-vocabulary slots and ships no members — how a project declares its own emotions, actions, anchors, costumes, camera framings and moves, transitions, CG layouts, sequences, music playback, moods, VFX types and text styles, the three declaration routes and their precedence, and the exits:/default: member semantics.
- [Dialogue & cast](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/dialogue-and-cast/): Content lines — the @speaker syntax for dialogue and narration — plus document sections and their stable ids, the declared cast that closes the set of speakers (with per-speaker presence and emotions), delivery flags and the mono point-of-view rule, line attributes and voice keys, interpolation and ordinals, inline text modifiers, and display names.
- [Core directives](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/directives/): The thirteen lute.core directives — ten staging leaves (::bg, ::music, ::sfx, ::actor, ::clear, ::camera, ::cg, ::vfx, ::video, ::sequence), the walk terminator ::end, and the forward jump pair ::jump / ::label — with their attributes, the project-declared staging vocabulary, attribute quoting, timing keys, the wait blocking model, and the when= guard.
- [Branch, match & when](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/branch-match-when/): The logic layer — player-driven <branch> menus and state-driven <match>/<when>/<otherwise> arms, with literal patterns, CEL guards, first-match-wins, and exhaustiveness.
- [Choices & hubs](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/choices-and-hubs/): Choice mechanics — when guards and the into= run-record sugar — plus revisit <hub> conversations with once/exit flags, hub prompts, and the no-dead-end guarantee.
- [Timeline & property tracks](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/timeline-and-property-tracks/): The <timeline> multi-track choreography block — a local clock, subject/channel/property tracks, absolute at offsets, and the one-writer-per-track rule.
- [Components & extends](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/components-and-extends/): Two reuse mechanisms — reusable content components invoked with ::use, including string params that carry a sentence into each call site, speaker params a body speaks as with @@who, param defaults, a body that reads its own plugin directive results, guarded ::use, and effects components that write state — and extends schema composition with base-layer override precedence.
- [Definitions & params](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/params/): Named typed CEL macros declared in defs, referenced as @name, and parameterized as @name(args) — the reusable-value layer of the language.
- [Quests & scenes](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/quests-and-scenes/): The time-axis document kinds — scenes sequenced with after:, and quests with objectives, derived completion, run, user, or season tiers, rearm conditions that run a quest again, and lifecycle-event reactions — beside the lore kind for looked-up content.
- [Lore entries](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/lore-entries/): The lore document kind — <entry> declarations the engine looks up instead of plays: item descriptions, found notes, inscriptions, codex pages, and barks, with state-dependent text and knowledge revealed through facts — and the <beat> blocks that bundle short scene beats beside them.
- [Beats](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/beats/): Scenes, lore entries, and bundled <beat> blocks that answer engine occasions — the scene frontmatter keys on, target, when, priority, once, also, spentBy, and for, the entry attributes on=, priority=, once=, spentBy=, and for=, beat bundles in a lore document, occasion target domains and kind targets, once-per-member beats (for=), occasion payloads, select: first / all / sequence, how eligible beats are ordered and presented, and what the checker proves about them (E-BEAT-ATTR, E-OCCASION-UNKNOWN, E-BEAT-UNREACHABLE, W-BEAT-SHADOWED, W-BEAT-PRIORITY-TIE, W-BEAT-ONCE-RUN-USER, W-ENTRY-WRITE-REREAD).
- [The clock](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/clock/): A declared day clock (dsl 0.24.0 §1) — the schema's clock: over engine-owned paths (day, optional slot and slots, raise as one occasion or a slot / dayStart / dayEnd map, week), day-granular clocks, what E-CLOCK-DECL rejects, the read-only clock.index / clock.weekday / clock.weekdayLabel, once: day, once: week (dsl 0.27.0) and once: slot beats and entries, moving time with lute play's advance: and include: steps, the lute calendar clock axis — and the three pieces that shipped beside it: enum member display labels, integer %, and the guarded write ::set{… when=…}.
- [Imports (uses:)](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/language/imports/): How a scene imports its shared state schema with uses:, the plain-YAML .schema.yaml declaration files, and the DAG discipline shared by uses / extends / components.
- [The state model](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/state/state-model/): Lute's tiered scalar state — the run, user, and app lifetime namespaces (plus episode-local scene and schema-declared season tiers), how paths are declared (including enum-typed and per-entity paths), the path-sensitive definite-assignment rules that govern reads and writes, the paths only the engine writes, and prev.run / prev.season, the previous run's or season window's final values.
- [Facts and Datalog](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/state/facts-and-datalog/): The relational fact layer beside Lute's scalar tiers — declared entities, sub-kinds and relations, relations that exclude each other (excludes:), ground facts asserted and retracted as deltas, and a total Datalog derivation layer that stays terminating by construction.
- [CEL expressions](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/state/cel/): The restricted Lute-CEL profile — the closed environment behind every condition and assignment, where it appears, the fact-query surface it admits, and how it compiles to inline CEL strings.
- [State schemas](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/state/schemas/): The shared, imported source of truth for run/user/app state, defs, entities, the cast, the clock, seasons and the end of the game — the schema document shape, and how uses composes peers while extends refines a base layer.
- [The scene graph and after:](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/connectivity/scene-graph/): How Lute assembles a project-wide prerequisite graph from each document's after declaration, the restricted visited/completed/active formula grammar, and the lute scenario graph view with its per-edge atom kinds and its bundle beat nodes.
- [Reachability](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/connectivity/reachability/): How Lute proves whether a node has a satisfiable route under the declared after graph, the Reachable / Unreachable / Unknown verdicts, per-node cycle degradation, and lute scenario reach.
- [Guaranteed / Possible envelopes](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/connectivity/envelopes/): The per-node available-state analysis — the Guaranteed and Possible tables over run/user state, the guaranteed-facts table beside them, why active(Q) is strictly weaker than completed(Q), the Possible-minus-Guaranteed warning, and quest addressing including the bare-quest defaults-only answer.
- [CLI reference](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/cli/): Every lute subcommand — init, new, check, check-project, compile, compile-stream, run, play, trace, test, lint, scenario, beats, calendar, refs, loc, context, tag, fix, lore, doctor, catalog refresh, version — with its synopsis, key flags, and exit-code contract.
- [Impact and constraints (0.34.0)](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/cli/#impact): `lute impact <dir> <target>` computes a transitive reverse-dependency closure for `state:`, `fact:`, `relation:`, `scene:`, `quest:`, `objective:`, `entry:`, `beat:`, `occasion:`, `def:`, and `component:` targets. JSON items carry declaration `file`/`line` when known; line items additionally carry `lineId` and `speaker`. `lute constraints <dir> [--run]` reports every `reachable`, `completable`, `speaksOnlyWhen`, and `noSingleSlotProgress` verdict from manifest `constraints:` declarations. Results use evidence `proven`, `witnessed`, `bounded`, `heuristic`, and `unknown`.
- [Evidence and project model (0.34.0)](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/cli/#evidence-levels): Project commands share one model per nearest manifest root. `trace`, `play`, `test`, `calendar`, `scenario`, and `beats` expose evidence fields; human output scopes bounded/heuristic/unknown claims and never says “no path exists” for a bounded search.
- [Playing a story](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/play/): Occasions and beats (dsl 0.21.0) — how a project says which piece of story answers which engine moment — and `lute play`, the reference player that walks a scripted playthrough through a whole project: raised occasions, the engine's own writes, a save to start from, and assertions `lute test` runs (dsl 0.22.0); occasions that play a whole sequence, side remarks, deadlines, targeted objectives, and beat bundles (dsl 0.23.0); a clock the script advances, answers for plugin bridge calls, and quest structure in the transcript (dsl 0.24.0); a clock advanced to a named slot or weekday, quests the engine accepts, and beats that answer a whole kind (dsl 0.26.0).
- [Story overviews](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/overviews/): Three read-only views of a story chosen by occasions (dsl 0.23.0): `lute beats` prints each occasion's beat ladder with the checker's verdicts, `lute calendar` evaluates play's own eligibility over a grid of state values, and `lute scenario knowledge` traces every fact-guarded condition through the rules to whatever produces its facts. Since 0.24.0: clock and visited axes, per-occasion axes, `--facts` tables and the never-presented list in the calendar, and defs as written with `--expand`. Since 0.26.0: covered fallbacks and kind ladders in `lute beats`, fact-producer edges in `lute scenario --facts`, and counted rule premises in `knowledge`.
- [Runtime contract](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/runtime-contract/): What a game engine must implement to run a compiled Lute artifact — the envelope, exact-minor IR and semantic negotiation, engine capability matrix, refusal-before-playback rule, and dispatcher loop over the scene and quest command kinds.
- [Engine integration 0.33](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/runtime-contract/): `requiredSemantics` is compiler-derived in each artifact and the project index. A host checks the exact-minor IR line first, then `lute.engine.yaml` `supportedIds`; `run`/`play` refuse missing ids before playback (`E-ENGINE-SEMANTICS`), while `check`/`check-project` report source spans (`E-CHECK-ENGINE-SEMANTICS`). The full semantic-id registry is in the 0.34.0 proposal.
- [Capability permissions](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/capability-permissions/): Restrict authored directives, state and fact writes, bridges, rewards, and quests with project profiles or a trusted host permission profile—without mistaking compile-time admission for a runtime sandbox.
- [Streaming continuation compiler](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/continuation-compiler/): Append ordinary Lute section-body text to a checked scene template, receive flushed full-artifact snapshots with lute compile-stream, and preserve runtime cursor and state correctly.
- [Tracing guide](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/tracing/): Preview a scene before you ship it — seeding state, facts, choices, events, accepts, the visited set, a save's quest status and entry reads, raised occasions (for a target, too), the previous run and plugin bridge answers via flags or a mock YAML file, credited rewards and objective bodies, quest structure, presenting one bundle beat or a kind beat's member, how the project's rules derive over them, reading the decision transcript (def references as authored, or `--expand`ed; a taken `::jump` followed to its label), and the E-TRACE-* refusals.
- [Linting](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/linting/): lute lint — advisory, per-project editorial lints (L-* codes) configured in lute.lint.yaml: the seven core rules, project-local custom rules, plugin lint exports, the metric tables rules read, the display-name advisory W-DISPLAY-NAME-DUP (dsl 0.26.0), and the exit-code contract.
- [Providers and catalog](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/providers-and-catalog/): Snapshot-first provider resolution — why the checker never depends on a live catalog, the --providers flag, catalog refresh re-stamping, and capabilitySnapshot.
- [Editors and LSP](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/editors/): Editor support for .lute — installing lute-lsp, wiring clients, sharing project/plugin/capability-permission diagnostics and completions with the CLI checker, and a server that notices its own binary was replaced.
- [AI harness guide](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/tooling/ai-harness/): Wiring Lute into an AI authoring pipeline — trusted permission-profile ceilings, filtered lute context, the lute check --json feedback loop, exit codes, diagnostics, and the proof-vs-review boundary.
- [Plugin concepts](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/plugins/concepts/): How Lute plugins extend vocabulary and capability surfaces without ever touching the fixed grammar or compiler behavior, and how every declaration they make is validated rather than trusted.
- [Manifests & resolution](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/plugins/manifests/): The plugin.yaml manifest and its export files, cross-cutting stampAttrs, declarative lowering to core staging records, and how installed plugins resolve deterministically into one capability snapshot.
- [Typed bridge directives](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/plugins/bridge/): How a plugin declares a typed runtime bridge, the directive that invokes it, the declared result state it writes, sync timing, and the match over its result slot.
- [Profiles & activation](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/plugins/profiles/): Selecting capability plugins with a source profile, layering typed options, and distinguishing activation from trusted project/host permission ceilings.

### Specification 0.39.0

- [Current specification](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/spec/current/): Current language and execution contract, including domain modules, semantic registry, `requiredSemantics`, engine matrices, exact-minor negotiation, and refusal diagnostics.
- [Specification index](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/spec/): Versioned proposal stack through 0.39.0, including the AI edit-loop and lossless source tooling release.

## Specification

- [Current specification](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/spec/current/): The consolidated index of what the Lute language and execution contract enforce today at version 0.39.0 — each language area mapped to the versioned proposal that introduced or last changed it, all pointing back to the normative repository sources.
- [Specification index](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/spec/): The versioned Lute spec stack — every scenario-DSL revision plus the plugin-system and character-cast capability proposals, with links to the normative repository sources.
- [Normative proposals](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute/tree/main/docs/proposals): The repository proposal files are the normative source of truth; the website is the readable companion.

## Optional

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/journeyWorker/lute): Source, issues, and the full history of the Lute language and toolchain.
- [Full-spec showcase](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/examples/showcase/): A walkthrough of the self-contained showcase project — a full-feature episode plus hub and when-is companions that drive the implemented language surface end-to-end and check clean under 0.9.0.
- [Example games](https://lute-lang.vercel.app/examples/games/): Fourteen complete games in the repository — mysteries, roguelikes, visual novels, live-ops, a gacha, an Ink port — each its own project, checked with zero warnings and run with its tests and plays in CI.

## 0.36.6 AI editing commands

`lute fmt [--check] <path>…` deterministically formats Lute-owned source;
YAML values are opaque. Exit 0 is canonical/success, 1 is noncanonical in
check mode, and 2 is I/O, UTF-8, or parse failure.

`lute diff <before> <after> --json` compares directories or `git:<rev>` sides
and returns `schemaVersion: "0.36.0.diff"`, `before`, `after`, and sorted
semantic `changes` (format-only changes return `[]`). Exit 2 rejects invalid
input or I/O failures.

`lute patch <dir> patch.json [--dry-run] --json` returns
`schemaVersion: "0.36.0.patch", ok, before, after, diff, writes`. Operations
are `replaceNode`, `insertBefore`, `insertAfter`, `replaceAttr`, `removeNode`,
`createFile`, `moveFile`, and revision-guarded `replaceText`. Preserve kinds
are `ids`, `lineIds`, `voiceKeys`, `choiceEffects`, `rewards`, `conditions`,
`reachability`, `hostContracts`, and `constraints`. Refusals exit 2:
`E-PATCH-STALE`, `E-PATCH-TARGET`, `E-PATCH-EDIT`, `E-PATCH-CHECK`, and
`E-PATCH-PRESERVE`.

`lute context <dir> --target <kind:key> --max-items N --json` or
`--at <file>:<line>:<column>` returns `schemaVersion`, `projectRevision`,
`files`, `target`, `declared`, `references`, `affected`, `tests`, `plays`,
`vocabulary`, and `notIncluded`; `--run <FILE>` requires a script and records
witnessed execution.

Lute 0.36 identity: authored `::use` instance keys, `identity.requireStable`,
`lute tag` back-fill, `identity.renames`/`identityRenames`, and `lute diff`
`renamed`/`unmappedIdentity` results are documented in the full reference.
